item.title: China welcomes foreign firms to deepen investment cooperation: vice premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 12 -- China welcomes companies from all countries, including Invesco, to further deepen investment cooperation with China for mutual benefit and win-win outcomes, Vice Premier He Lifeng said in Beijing Thursday. He, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while meeting with Andrew Schlossberg, president and chief executive officer of Invesco. He noted that China's economic momentum is turning toward innovation and its economic structure is improving, showing strong resilience and vitality. He said China is advancing high-quality development of its financial sector in line with its plans and expanding high-level financial opening-up. Schlossberg said he is optimistic about China's economic prospects and is willing to continue deepening engagement in the Chinese market to expand pragmatic cooperation.

item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday. The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said. The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech. President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added.

item.title: Chinese premier calls for improving multi-tiered social security system
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
BEIJING, Nov. 12 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Thursday called for further deepening social security reform and improving a multi-tiered social security system that covers the entire population in both urban and rural areas and is fair and unified, safe and well-regulated, and sustainable. Li made the remarks while presiding over a State Council study session on improving the multi-tiered social security system and further strengthening the social security safety net. China has basically established the world's largest and fully functional social security system. Yet changes in the demographic structure, technological progress and diverse forms of employment have placed new and higher demands on the development of the social security system, Li said. He noted that the country must proceed from its own realities, balance doing the best with doing what is possible, and raise social security levels steadily as the economy develops. Li also underlined the need to clarify the responsibilities of the government, employers, individuals and society, so that responsibilities are properly shared and a long-term mechanism of mutual assistance is formed. While meeting basic needs and providing a safety net, the system should offer more varied forms of provision to meet people's multi-tiered and diverse needs. He called for accelerating efforts to address weak links, expand coverage of enterprise annuities, make the personal pension scheme more attractive, support the growth of commercial health insurance, and steadily advance the long-term care insurance system. He said greater attention should be given to people in flexible employment and new forms of employment, with improvements to their social security arrangements, a gradual increase in participation rates, and stronger protection of their rights and interests. Li also highlighted the need to make the social security system fairer, steadily raise pension protection for urban and rural residents, make better use of unemployment insurance, improve the tiered and classified social assistance system, and refine the social welfare system. He added that supervision of the social security fund should be strengthened, the fund's value preserved and increased, and relevant laws and regulations revised in a timely manner to provide stronger legal support.

item.title: Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
BEIJING, Nov. 12 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Sun died in 1925. Thursday's gathering in the Great Hall of the People was attended by about 3,000 people, including senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. Wang presided over the event. Xi met with Sun's relatives and representatives of overseas guests before the event started. In his speech, Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution. He said that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. For more than 100 years, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said. "The best way for us to remember Dr. Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing our endeavors to build a great country and rejuvenate our nation," Xi said. Highlighting Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, Xi called on all Chinese people to learn from Sun and promote patriotism to strive for a strong and prosperous China. He also lauded Sun's dedication to the people, underscoring the imperative of always putting the people first and serving them wholeheartedly. On the new journey, it is essential to make solid headway in promoting well-rounded personal development and common prosperity for all, Xi stressed. Noting that Sun devoted his life to the pursuit of truth, Xi stressed the need to learn from Sun's example, advance theoretical exploration and innovation with courage, and continue to write new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. Xi called on the Chinese people to carry forward Sun's unyielding determination, rise to challenges ahead and break new ground in the country's development. "We must carry forward the fighting spirit, build up our ability, be ready to withstand high winds, choppy waters, and even dangerous storms, and overcome all the risks and challenges we face on the way forward," Xi said. Calling on people to learn from Sun's commitment to unity, Xi also emphasized adhering to the united front and strengthening the great unity among all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. Highlighting Sun's global vision, Xi called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. "Dr. Sun always upheld national unity and ethnic solidarity, and resolutely opposed any word or act attempting to split the country and divide the nation," Xi said. Resolving the Taiwan question and realizing the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi stressed. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and all Chinese at home and abroad should join hands to oppose the "Taiwan independence" secessionist forces, and work together for the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland, Xi said. "On the basis of adhering to the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, we are willing to engage in dialogue and consultations with people of vision and insight from all sectors in Taiwan on matters related to cross-Strait relations and national reunification," Xi said. "We will definitely give full consideration to Taiwan's realities and take full account of the interests and feelings of our compatriots in Taiwan," Xi said. "But we will never leave any room for 'Taiwan independence' separatist activities in any form." "The historical trends are unstoppable. The complete reunification of our motherland must be realized, and it can, without doubt, be realized," Xi said.

item.title: Chinese vice premier stresses sustained improvement in industrial innovation capacity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
SHANGHAI, Nov. 10 -- Chinese Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing has stressed the need to steadily advance the deep integration of technological and industrial innovation and to continuously enhance industrial innovation capabilities to better support high-quality economic development. Zhang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during an inspection tour in Shanghai, east China, on Monday and Tuesday. During the tour, Zhang visited instrumentation and medical equipment enterprises and learned about their operations. He emphasized the need to better align high-quality sci-tech supply with industrial demand and to use high-end, green and intelligent industrial needs to guide sci-tech innovation, so that innovation outcomes are translated into real productivity faster. He also called for stronger basic research and breakthroughs in advanced basic processes, key basic materials and basic components, better mechanisms for translating research into application and related services, and a sound innovation ecosystem in which enterprises of all sizes and along industrial chains collaborate. Noting that traditional industries remain a foundation for economic growth and employment, Zhang stressed advancing the application of advanced technologies to empower traditional industries and promote their high-quality development. During discussions with grassroots officials and enterprise representatives, Zhang called for creating new consumption scenarios, improving the consumption environment and expanding quality products and services to promote consumption upgrading. He urged better combining investment in physical facilities with institutional and service improvements, stepping up project planning and preparation, and advancing major projects suited to local conditions. Zhang also called for further advancing the development of a unified national market and intensifying efforts to curb "involution-style" competition, so as to foster a fair and orderly market environment.

item.title: Chinese premier to visit Thailand, travel to Philippines for China-ASEAN summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
BEIJING, Nov. 11 -- At the invitation of Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, Chinese Premier Li Qiang will pay an official visit to Thailand from Nov. 13 to 15, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Wednesday. At the invitation of President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. of the Philippines, the rotating chair of ASEAN, Premier Li will attend the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila from Nov. 15 to 16, the spokesperson added.

item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses.

item.title: Chinese premier signs decree to revise, repeal certain administrative regulations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
BEIJING, Nov. 5 -- A decision by China's State Council to amend and repeal certain administrative regulations was made public on Thursday. Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating the decision, which aims to address pointless formalities to lighten the burden on those working on the ground, implement the reform of Party and state institutions, and ensure the consistency of relevant laws and regulations. Certain provisions of 14 administrative regulations were revised, and four regulations were repealed, according to the document. The State Council decided to revise a regulation on river course administration to align it with related provisions in the country's Ecological and Environmental Code. Meanwhile, a regulation on the limits of liability for maritime passenger transport between Chinese ports was repealed to better meet the needs of ongoing reform and development, and address practical realities in relevant areas. The decision takes effect on the date of its promulgation.
